question: Do the remaining bad primes expose exceptional quotient directions, separately or jointly, in the three frozen high/low pairs?
cases: The six rows, in order, in rank_jump_bad_prime_inputs_v1.json; no new candidate selection.
method: Factor the discriminant of each retained integral short model, retaining trial factors before a bounded completion attempt. Compute local Kummer signatures only at certified odd support primes above 13. Combine with the retained 2,3,5,7,11,13,infinity signatures. Local minimal reduction distinguishes genuine bad places from nonminimal-model factors.

endpoints.positive: A nonzero quotient image identifies local or joint support of known exceptional classes; it does not prove unseen incidence or solubility.
endpoints.negative: A complete all-bad-place generic image excludes an additional-support explanation at those places. It is not a full Selmer group or a global-divisibility test.
endpoints.failure: Timeouts leave factorization or local coverage UNKNOWN. Preserve partial prime factors and omit any completeness claim. Never increase limits to complete a case.

reproducibility: One factor checkpoint and one local checkpoint per curve; isolated rank-jump paths; exact factor products and local signatures replayable.
